LESSON: LISTENING AND SPEAKING 9.1.1 LANGUAGE STRATEGIES ON DAILY EXPERIENCES

Grade: Grade 5
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
Strand: Strand 9
Topic 9.1: Listening and Speaking 9.1.1 Language Strategies on Daily Experiences
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Listening and Speaking 9.1.1 Language Strategies on Daily Experiences, part of Strand 9 in Grade 5 INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES.

Key inquiry question: Why do we celebrate national days? 2. How can we describe an event interestingly?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. describe national events fluently and with expression,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Listening and Speaking 9.1.1 Language Strategies on Daily Experiences in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. compose songs based on patriotism for expression,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Listening and Speaking 9.1.1 Language Strategies on Daily Experiences in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. value the place of national days in promoting ethnic cohesion.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Listening and Speaking 9.1.1 Language Strategies on Daily Experiences in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. describe national events fluently and with expression,

   Listening and Speaking 9.1.1 Language Strategies on Daily Experiences helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

B. compose songs based on patriotism for expression,

   Listening and Speaking 9.1.1 Language Strategies on Daily Experiences helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

C. value the place of national days in promoting ethnic cohesion.

   Listening and Speaking 9.1.1 Language Strategies on Daily Experiences helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

D. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. listen to and watch recorded events on national days,

2. work collaboratively to build a vocabulary bank on words related to national days,

3. work jointly with peers to describe the events and activities fluently, with accuracy and with expression,

4. listen to each other describing events and identify adverbs used,

5. work collaboratively to compose patriotic songs for a national day,

6. team up with peers to perform the patriotic songs during an indigenous day interclass festival. 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. listen to and watch recorded events on national days,
2. work collaboratively to build a vocabulary bank on words related to national days,
3. work jointly with peers to describe the events and activities fluently, with accuracy and with expression,
4. listen to each other describing events and identify adverbs used,
5. work collaboratively to compose patriotic songs for a national day,
6. team up with peers to perform the patriotic songs during an indigenous day interclass festival. 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Listening and Speaking 9.1.1 Language Strategies on Daily Experiences together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Citizenship: This is enhanced as the learner works collaboratively with peers to compose patriotic songs to show love for

their country.

• Communication and Collaboration: This is developed as the learner engages actively when listening to each other describing

events and identifying adverbs used.

Values:
• Unity: This is acquired as the learner works collaboratively to build a vocabulary bank on words related to national days.

• Patriotism: This is enhanced as the learner teams up with peers to perform the patriotic songs during an indigenous day

interclass festival.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Ethnic and racial relations: This is promoted as the learner is exposed to content on patriotism and nationalism through patriotic

songs.

Link to other Learning Areas:

The learner can relate the concept nationalism and patriotism to their learning of unity in Social Studies.
